result:
You're right, and I'll keep this short. There's one decision left before I write it up: how it gets built. Your answers settled what it does. They don't yet settle where it lives.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** Batch tracking becomes its own section of the Flask app already on the Pi, with its own tables in the same SQLite database.
- The sack scanner works as a plain USB barcode reader, and the label printer runs from the Pi.
- **Gain:** one thing to run, update, and back up. It's the setup you already know works.
- **Cost:** the brewery and the taproom share one app. A bad update to the brew-day pages could take the tabs down on a busy night, unless we're careful about how changes go out.

**2. Build a separate small app on the same Pi.** Same tools, but its own program and its own database file.
- **Gain:** the taproom and the brewhouse can't break each other.
- **Cost:** two services to keep running and two databases to back up, on a machine that's also in the office.

I also considered off-the-shelf brewery software that already does lot tracing. I set it aside because you're paying monthly for something you've described exactly, and it wouldn't drive your label printer the way you want.

I recommend option 1. Your operation is one Pi and one person maintaining it. Keeping the code in its own clearly separated section of the app gets you most of the safety of option 2 at half the upkeep.

This is a full write-up rather than a quick change, so it goes into the project as a document. Before I hand it to you, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer.

Which way do you want to go, 1 or 2?
